spans.claim: Sir Alan Hume-Frazer was found dead outside the library window
spans.anchor: found his young master stretched on the turf at the side of the drive
spans.span: To his dismay he found his young master stretched on the turf at the side of the drive, thirty feet from the house.

spans.claim: David Hume-Frazer was asleep in the library at 1 a.m.
spans.anchor: Mr. David Hume-Frazer was curled up in an arm-chair asleep
spans.span: Mr. David Hume-Frazer was curled up in an arm-chair asleep, or rather dozing, for he stirred a little when the man put some coal in the grate.

spans.claim: The Japanese Ko-Katana was the murder weapon
spans.anchor: The dagger-like attachment to your Japanese sword had been driven into his breast up to the hilt
spans.span: The dagger-like attachment to your Japanese sword had been driven into his breast up to the hilt, actually splitting his heart.

spans.claim: The drawer in Sir Alan's writing desk was forcibly opened
spans.anchor: a small drawer in Sir Alan's writing-table had been wrenched open whilst you were alone in the room
spans.span: Then, again, a small drawer in Sir Alan's writing-table had been wrenched open whilst you were alone in the room.

spans.claim: A man resembling David was seen near Beechcroft at night
spans.anchor: a man was running at top speed, with the labouring breath of one unaccustomed to the exercise

spans.claim: Numagawa Jiro identified the Japanese motto on the Ko-Katana
spans.anchor: I have nothing to tell. I told the police all that they asked me

spans.claim: Mrs. Jiro dressed in male attire to warn Ooma
spans.anchor: Mrs. Jiro forthwith seated herself to listen to the conclave
spans.span: Mrs. Jiro forthwith seated herself to listen to the conclave.

spans.claim: Ooma sent Jiro to Ipswich to watch the trial
spans.anchor: He sent Jiro to Ipswich to attend Mr. David's second trial
spans.span: He sent Jiro to Ipswich to attend Mr. David's second trial when the first missed fire.

spans.claim: Robert Hume-Frazer was attacked and nearly killed in London
spans.anchor: Mr. Robert Hume-Frazer quitted his hotel for a stroll in the West End, and narrowly escaped being run over in Whitehall
spans.span: Early in the morning, Mr. Robert Hume-Frazer quitted his hotel for a stroll in the West End, and narrowly escaped being run over in Whitehall.

spans.claim: Ooma killed Giovanni Capella by throwing him from a train
spans.anchor: I took the little man and cracked his neck. Then I flung him over the bridge
spans.span: I looked out of the window and saw that we were coming to a viaduct over a stream between deep cliffs, so I took the little man and cracked his neck. Then I flung him over the bridge.

spans.claim: Ooma barricaded himself in the library and was confronted
spans.anchor: Ooma barricaded by the table, the others ready to defeat any stratagem he might endeavour to put in force
spans.span: Thus, in a segment of a circle, the five enclosed the one against the wall--Ooma barricaded by the table, the others ready to defeat any stratagem he might endeavour to put in force.

spans.claim: Ooma injected himself with snake poison during arrest
spans.anchor: He folded his arms and looked at them. A change came over his face
spans.span: He folded his arms and looked at them. A change came over his face.

spans.claim: The family secret involved Margaret's illegitimate birth
spans.anchor: I am a nameless outcast. My mother was not Alan's mother
spans.span: In the eyes of the law I am a nameless outcast. My mother was not Alan's mother.

spans.claim: The typewritten anonymous letter was written by Ooma via Jiro
spans.anchor: The letter which I made Jiro write for me. He wrote it badly

spans.claim: The stationmaster saw a third David Hume on New Year's Eve
spans.anchor: I fancied I saw Mr. David leave the London train due here at 12.15 midday
spans.span: On the morning of December 31, I fancied I saw Mr. David leave the London train due here at 12.15 midday.

spans.claim: Ooma is a Japanese descendant of the original David Hume
spans.anchor: I am his lawful descendant. I came to England and resolved to be an Englishman
spans.span: I am his lawful descendant. I came to England and resolved to be an Englishman.

spans.claim: The Ko-Katana bore a Japanese motto linked to Ooma's family
spans.anchor: Beneath the rust on the blade he thought he could distinguish some Japanese characters
spans.span: Beneath the rust on the blade he thought he could distinguish some Japanese characters in the quaint pictorial script adapted by that singular people from the Chinese system of writing.

spans.claim: Ooma confessed to the murders before dying
spans.anchor: I killed Capella. It was a mistake. Everything is a mistake
spans.span: I killed Capella. It was a mistake. Everything is a mistake.

spans.claim: The library window was the scene of the murder
